newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Tutu has cancerous prostate removed.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Tutu has cancerous prostate removed.

text.p: South African Nobel peace prize winner Archbishop Desmond Tutu has had surgery to remove a cancerous prostate gland, a spokeswoman said on Friday.
Christelle Terblanche said initial tests on Tutu, 65, who was admitted to a Cape Town hospital on Wednesday, had indicated no malignancy.
"(But) the archbishop's urologist proceeded with a full prostate operation and removed the bulk of the prostate. Further tests were carried out on the removed tissues.
"The results of these tests have indicated a definite cancer of the prostate but further tests will be needed to determine the extent and its seriousness.

"There's nothing to suggest cancer outside the prostate at this stage," Terblanche said, adding: "The urologist does not believe it helpful to become involved in speculative comment about the prognosis."
Tutu, who stepped down as Anglican archbishop of Southern Africa in June last year, told reporters from his hospital bed:
"I have full confidence in the people looking after me."
He said the work of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, of which he is chairman, would not be affected.
The commission was set up by President Nelson Mandela to investigate the crimes and human rights violations under apartheid.

Tutu is working to persuade politicians as well as police officers and old soldiers to apply for amnesty for apartheid atrocities from the commission, calling it South Africa's last chance to heal the past.

"There is no instrument with the same potential for ending the accusations and counter-accusations, the recriminations and political bickering which will plague this country for generations to come, if you do not seize the opportunity," he said in December last year.
